title: Cycle Playbook: Dynamic Staffing Shifts and Scoped Decomposition Runbook
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Purpose: Provide a pragmatic, reproducible playbook for PMs and Eng leads to (1) shift headcount temporarily across initiatives when a cycle experiences unplanned slippage, and (2) rapidly decompose and trim scope to preserve mission-critical outcomes. This ticket captures the runbook, measurable triggers, decision authority, and communication templates for stakeholder alignment.

Background: Our recent cycles showed uneven load across teams and ad-hoc scope cuts that caused rework and missed OKR outcomes. We need a documented process that balances predictable commit economics with the reality of mid-cycle variance: staff out-of-band reassignments, short-duration float pools, and surgical scope reductions.

Goals:
- Reduce last-minute all-hands scope churn that increases rework by >25%
- Ensure critical platform/SLA work remains funded when features slip
- Make transient staff shifts transparent and time-boxed (<= 4 weeks)
- Provide clear, low-friction templates for PM/Eng/Design to execute cuts or swaps

Principles:
- Prefer short, reversible staffing moves (<= 4 weeks) over permanent reassignments
- Prioritize customer-facing or security/regulatory work before nice-to-have UX polish
- Scoped cuts should preserve an end-to-end vertical if possible (thin slice)
- Limit cascading dependencies by identifying and freezing non-essential upstream work

Runbook (high level):
1) Trigger detection: PM flags a slippage if two of these are met: velocity burn > 20% vs plan, unplanned critical bug spike (>= 5 Sev2+), or blocking infra incident affecting >1 business unit.
2) Rapid capacity assessment (48 hours): Eng manager provides headcount availability, skillset map, and minimum buffer for on-call/infra. Product lead lists top 3 candidate features for scoping down.
3) Decision meeting (2 hours): PM + Eng manager + Design lead + TPM + Head of Product meet to select between options: (A) temporary headcount reassign, (B) scope shave, (C) split milestone with reduced MVR/alpha. Record decision and owner.
4) Execution steps: If staffing move, create a time-boxed assignment ticket, update staffing roster, notify HR for compensation/allocations if >4 weeks. If scope shave, create trimmed Acceptance Criteria and identify blocked components to freeze.
5) Communication: Use standardized templates (stakeholder email, public roadmap update, Slack #announce). Budget a follow-up review 2 weeks after restore to capture retrospective.

Acceptance criteria:
- A documented decision and owner exists in the cycle board within 48 hours of trigger
- Any staffing move is accompanied by a clear handback plan (owner, exact date, knowledge transfer checklist)
- Scope trims include explicit acceptance criteria and test plan to avoid regressions
- All affected customers or internal stakeholders are notified within 24 hours

Metrics & signals to monitor:
- Cycle velocity delta vs plan (weekly)
- Number of scope-cut items reintroduced in the next cycle (target <= 10%)
- Mean time for staff reassignment (target <= 48 hours from decision to assignment)
- Customer-visible incidents tied to trimmed areas (target: none)

Stakeholders and roles:
- Product lead (decision owner): Priya Shah
- Engineering lead (capacity owner): Alex Morgan
- Design lead (UX impact assessment): Mei Tan
- TPM (execution coordinator): Diego Alvarez
- People Ops (if reassignment >4 weeks): Laura Chen

Templates attached (examples in comments): standardized decision summary, stakeholder email, roadmap blurb, and handback checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Decision & owner recorded in cycle board within 48 hours
Handback plan and KT checklist for any reassigned headcount
Trimmed scope has clear acceptance criteria and test plan
Stakeholders notified within 24 hours of decision
decisions: Favor reversible, time-boxed staffing shifts over permanent reassignments
Preserve at least a thin vertical for customer-facing flows when cutting scope
